answer: A concrete defense is a crystal work ledger: every identity must carve one cedar tag per epoch into a shared glacier registry, and the tag must cover fresh work verified by two randomly drawn peers. Reused geometry collapses into the original identity and merges rewards, so cloned agents cannot amortize a single proof. Each tag is priced at 0.04 compute-hours per epoch, and k identities must carve k distinct tags; the chain cannot be reset or parallelized without new verified work, keeping marginal cost linear in n.
